projectDesc.p: Encoded for the Experiencing War web site for the Veterans History Project.

samplingDecl.p: The recording of the interview with Dennis Chastain was digitized.

editorialDecl.p: This transcription was encoded with minimal changes to the original text in an effort to preserve original content and idiosyncrasies of the person interviewed. Period language and terminology are also retained. Encoding is literal with regard to the transcriptionist's capitalization, punctuation, and spelling.

sp.speaker: Adam Roenfeldt
sp.p: This is Saturday, April 2, 2005 and this is the beginning of the interview with Dennis Chastain at his home at 10800 Crystal Hill Road in Maumelle, Arkansas. Mr. Chastain is 89 years old, having been bom on September 10,1915. Our names are Adam Roenfeldt and Kristin Dietrich and we are the reporters. Dennis Chastain is Kristin's great-grandfather on her dad's side. Dennis, could you state for the recording, what war and branch you served in? What was your rank, and where did you serve?

sp.speaker: Adam Roenfeldt
sp.p: Were you drafted or did you enlist?

sp.speaker: Dennis Chastain
sp.p: I, I was drafted

sp.speaker: Adam Roenfeldt
sp.p: Where were you living at the time?

sp.speaker: Dennis Chastain
sp.p: North Little Rock

sp.speaker: Adam Roenfeldt
sp.p: Why did you join? Why did you join the Army?

sp.speaker: Dennis Chastain
sp.p: Why did I join?

sp.speaker: Adam Roenfeldt
sp.p: Mhm.

sp.speaker: Dennis Chastain
sp.p: Well, I wanted in anyhow. So, I just let them draft me.

sp.speaker: Adam Roenfeldt
sp.p: Do you recall the first days of your service?

sp.speaker: Dennis Chastain
sp.p: Do I recall the first day? Yeah, we went to Shreveport, Louisiana.

sp.speaker: Adam Roenfeldt
sp.p: What did it feel like?

sp.speaker: Dennis Chastain
sp.p: That was an induction center.

sp.speaker: Adam Roenfeldt
sp.p: Do you remember your instructors, your instructors? Okay, do you remember who your instructors were?

sp.speaker: Dennis Chastain
sp.p: No, I don't remember the instructions. I, I cant hear you.

sp.speaker: Adam Roenfeldt
sp.p: Okay.

sp.speaker: Dennis Chastain
sp.p: I cant understand your words

sp.speaker: Adam Roenfeldt
sp.p: Which wars did you serve in? Like, uh, which war? Which war did you serve in? Did you serve in World War II or the Korean, or Vietnam?

sp.speaker: Dennis Chastain
sp.p: World War II.

sp.speaker: Adam Roenfeldt
sp.p: You served in World War II? Where did you go in World War II?

sp.speaker: Dennis Chastain
sp.p: Uh, I went to the army basic camp in Alabama.

sp.speaker: Adam Roenfeldt
sp.p: Do you remember arriving in Alabama?

sp.speaker: Dennis Chastain
sp.p: Yeah.

sp.speaker: Adam Roenfeldt
sp.p: Could you tell me what it was like there?

sp.speaker: Dennis Chastain
sp.p: Night? It was day time I think.

sp.speaker: Adam Roenfeldt
sp.p: What was your job in Alabama base?

sp.speaker: Dennis Chastain
sp.p: I was a trainee and a tank maintenance.

sp.speaker: Adam Roenfeldt
sp.p: So you were a maintenance guy on the tanks?

sp.speaker: Dennis Chastain
sp.p: Yeah.

sp.speaker: Adam Roenfeldt
sp.p: Where did you go after your training camp?

sp.speaker: Dennis Chastain
sp.p: I went to Kentucky.

sp.speaker: Adam Roenfeldt
sp.p: Went to Kentucky? Uh, Where did fight? Did you fight in the east, the pacific?

sp.speaker: Dennis Chastain
sp.p: Yeah.

sp.speaker: Adam Roenfeldt
sp.p: You fought in the Pacific?

sp.speaker: Dennis Chastain
sp.p: Yeah. The Pacific.

sp.speaker: Adam Roenfeldt
sp.p: When you were in the Pacific, did you see any combat D Yeah, I did.

sp.speaker: Adam Roenfeldt
sp.p: Do you remember if there were any casualties to your unit, or if anyone died in your unit?

sp.speaker: Dennis Chastain
sp.p: Oh yeah, I can remember some got killed later in the, in Lou don. We invaded, my unit invaded Manila. There was a Japanese occupying, we invaded Manila, we invaded and took over the city in Manila.

sp.speaker: Adam Roenfeldt
sp.p: Do you. What else do you remember from taking over Manila? Like what were some of your most memorable-like what were some of your experiences?

sp.speaker: Dennis Chastain
sp.p: Oh, I had a lot of tank tactics operations here and there. I guess Japanese. Up and down the, uh, the invasion of the Manila Strait.

sp.speaker: Adam Roenfeldt
sp.p: Um, uh. Did you ever get captured or uh, were you mostly safe?

sp.speaker: Dennis Chastain
sp.p: I was just an ordinary soldier.

sp.speaker: Adam Roenfeldt
sp.p: Alright, uh, did you ever get any medals or special honors?

sp.speaker: Dennis Chastain
sp.p: Some, but right now I do not recall what they are.

sp.speaker: Adam Roenfeldt
sp.p: Alright, um while you were in the war, did you stay in touch with your family (repeat) Write letters?

sp.speaker: Dennis Chastain
sp.p: Write Letters?

sp.speaker: Adam Roenfeldt
sp.p: Yeah, write letters.

sp.speaker: Dennis Chastain
sp.p: Well, I wrote letters all the time to my wife.

sp.speaker: Adam Roenfeldt
sp.p: Do you remember what the food was like in the military?

sp.speaker: Dennis Chastain
sp.p: Remember what?

sp.speaker: Adam Roenfeldt
sp.p: The food. Do you remember what you ate, like, do you remember the food? How it tasted?

sp.speaker: Dennis Chastain
sp.p: Oh no, it was so varied, I couldn't tell you.

sp.speaker: Adam Roenfeldt
sp.p: Um, did your unit have a lot of supplies?

sp.speaker: Dennis Chastain
sp.p: We did eat a lot of dog biscuits

sp.speaker: Adam Roenfeldt
sp.p: Um, while you were in the war, were you stressed or under pressure?

sp.speaker: Dennis Chastain
sp.p: No, not necessarily. Just unit pressure.

sp.speaker: Adam Roenfeldt
sp.p: Yeah. Did, was there something that gave you luck throughout the war? Like, did you have like a letter or something that you could be reminded of home? So that whenever...?

sp.speaker: Dennis Chastain
sp.p: No I cant think of anything.

sp.speaker: Adam Roenfeldt
sp.p: Okay, um do you remember how people spent their time like, entertaining themselves?

sp.speaker: Dennis Chastain
sp.p: The people that lived there?

sp.speaker: Adam Roenfeldt
sp.p: Yeah and the people in your group.

sp.speaker: Dennis Chastain
sp.p: Well I remember some, yeah its been a long time, its been sixty years. I am hazy. I'd have to get papers out; my discharge with all that kind of stuff.

sp.speaker: Adam Roenfeldt
sp.p: Ok um do you, when you were in the war do you remember anything really funny or really weird that happened?

sp.speaker: Dennis Chastain
sp.p: No not necessarily.

sp.speaker: Adam Roenfeldt
sp.p: What did you think of your fellow soldiers in the unit?

sp.speaker: Dennis Chastain
sp.p: My fellow soldiers were in the Ohio unit, I thought they were great soldiers because they were a unit of the National Guard; the Ohio.

sp.speaker: Adam Roenfeldt
sp.p: Do you remember anything that happened during the war? While you were in service, like getting under attack?

sp.speaker: Dennis Chastain
sp.p: Oh yeah, we got attacked a lot of times. By air and by land. Several of the guys I knew got killed in one wad one night by a bombing strafing. Stuff like that.

sp.speaker: Adam Roenfeldt
sp.p: Um, could you remember anymore stories?

sp.speaker: Dennis Chastain
sp.p: I didn't understand that.

sp.speaker: Adam Roenfeldt
sp.p: Do you have anymore stories? Do you remember anything else from the combat?

sp.speaker: Dennis Chastain
sp.p: Oh, no, not, not now.

sp.speaker: Adam Roenfeldt
sp.p: Not now? Do you remember the day that your service ended?

sp.speaker: Dennis Chastain
sp.p: Yeah.

sp.speaker: Adam Roenfeldt
sp.p: Can you tell me about that?

sp.speaker: Dennis Chastain
sp.p: The day the war ended?

sp.speaker: Adam Roenfeldt
sp.p: Yeah.

sp.speaker: Dennis Chastain
sp.p: Well, uh, that was a day of a, that Japan surrendered. That would be the topic. Of course, that was a world event and shown on TV and all that and I remember that day very well.

sp.speaker: Adam Roenfeldt
sp.p: Do you remember where you were that day?

sp.speaker: Dennis Chastain
sp.p: I was in the Phillipines about 50 miles from Manilla.

sp.speaker: Adam Roenfeldt
sp.p: After the war, when you got back to the United States, did you go to school or go back to work?

sp.speaker: Dennis Chastain
sp.p: Went back to work and school too.

sp.speaker: Adam Roenfeldt
sp.p: What was your job?

sp.speaker: Dennis Chastain
sp.p: I was a, uh, security officer at an ordinance plant.

sp.speaker: Adam Roenfeldt
sp.p: Um, you said you went back to school?

sp.speaker: Dennis Chastain
sp.p: Uh, yeah, I went to school at night.

sp.speaker: Adam Roenfeldt
sp.p: You went to school at night? Was your education supported by the G.I. Bill?

sp.speaker: Dennis Chastain
sp.p: I finished my High School education from 10th and, uh, uh, studied some other occupational things. Three or four of them, I think.

sp.speaker: Adam Roenfeldt
sp.p: Did you make a lot of friends while you were in the military?

sp.speaker: Dennis Chastain
sp.p: Yeah, all of them were my friends.

sp.speaker: Adam Roenfeldt
sp.p: After the war, did you see any of them again?

sp.speaker: Dennis Chastain
sp.p: Never seen them.

sp.speaker: Adam Roenfeldt
sp.p: Never saw them again? Did you join a veterans organization?

sp.speaker: Dennis Chastain
sp.p: Huh?

sp.speaker: Adam Roenfeldt
sp.p: Did you join a veterans organization?

sp.speaker: Adam Roenfeldt
sp.p: Can you tell me about that?

sp.speaker: Dennis Chastain
sp.p: Well, it was a post in, in located in Little Rock at the time. Ain't there anymore. It's all scattered and all gone now somewhere else. So I really don't remember anything else except that.

sp.speaker: Adam Roenfeldt
sp.p: When you were in the military-

sp.speaker: Dennis Chastain
sp.p: Never did write down anything to keep up with it. Actually, I became disassociated with American Legions while they disbanded that unit. Didn't keep up with my dues, I guess. Something.

sp.speaker: Adam Roenfeldt
sp.p: Um, in the, um. Veterans Organization, what type of activities did your post or association do?

sp.speaker: Dennis Chastain
sp.p: I didn't have any.

sp.speaker: Adam Roenfeldt
sp.p: Okay, um, how did getting in the military effect your life after the war?

sp.speaker: Dennis Chastain
sp.p: Well, I just worked from this category to that category in the army. Uh, when they played out and pulled me from them while I went to another one. I became a permanent employee of the Civil Service. And, uh, they transferred around.

sp.speaker: Adam Roenfeldt
sp.p: Is there anything else you would like to say about your time in the war?

sp.speaker: Dennis Chastain
sp.p: Um, nope. Not necessarily, now. I have the excerpts that I could record. I don't have the definite facts on it, like the papers and things like that now. I'll have to skip that now.

sp.speaker: Adam Roenfeldt
sp.p: Oh, okay. Well, um, thank you for being interviewed by us.

sp.speaker: Dennis Chastain
sp.p: Okay, your welcome.

sp.speaker: Adam Roenfeldt
sp.p: Thank you very much.
